claims.text: High-purity polycrystalline alumina is a predominantly insulating, phonon-dominated heat-conducting material with negligible electronic contributions.
Introducing short-range-order precipitates into alumina will decrease phonon scattering times.
Introducing short-range-order precipitates will reduce alumina's lattice thermal conductivity relative to homogeneous alumina.
Suitable doping and processing can create nanometer-scale ordered regions in alumina.
At low to moderate temperatures, phonon transport dominates in the proposed alumina samples and electronic conduction remains minimal.
The proposed intervention will produce nanometer-scale SRO precipitates embedded in the alumina matrix.
SRO precipitates act as additional phonon-scattering centers.
Scattering from SRO precipitates reduces phonon mean free paths.
Reduced phonon mean free paths and scattering times lower lattice thermal conductivity.
The extent of thermal-conductivity reduction depends on the density and size distribution of the SRO precipitates.
Extreme precipitate clustering or overly large precipitates may fail to produce the anticipated thermal-conductivity reduction.
Precipitate size, density, interfacial quality, and secondary effects influence the magnitude of the thermal-conductivity change.
